subject: Realtime API streaming slowdown: operational update and post-incident summary
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@fastchat.ai>
To: support@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-18T08:50:00Z
Subject: Realtime API: streaming responses ~1.5-3x slower since 2026-08-18 08:45 UTC

Hi Redwood team,

We're seeing a sustained increase in per-token latency for streaming responses from the Realtime endpoint starting 08:45 UTC. Typical token latency for our integration is ~20-30ms; since this morning it's consistently 40-90ms and some sessions are stalling mid-stream. This is impacting our live chat SLA for web clients.

We've already verified client-side network health and retried with exponential backoff; problem persists. Attaching a short recording and sample traces. Can you confirm whether there are platform-side degradations and any immediate mitigations we can apply on our side?

Impact: ~12% of sessions with user-perceivable lag, peak at 14:15 UTC.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Platform
FastChat.ai
attachments: fastchat_stream_capture.mp4 (video), sample_trace.json (text)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-18T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Realtime API: streaming responses ~1.5-3x slower since 2026-08-18 08:45 UTC

Hi Maya — thanks for the heads up and the captures. We're actively triaging. Immediate notes and short-term mitigations you can try while we investigate: 

- Toggle client-side: enable streamed-chunk-size=512 (smaller chunking reduces buffer pressure in some paths).
- Increase client-side stream read-timeout by +250ms to prevent perceived stalls while we remediate.
- If you have the ability to pin to a quantized model variant, try the lower-latency variant we surfaced last quarter (rwd-q4f); I can whitelist your project if needed.

We're pulling telemetry from edge shards and the continuous-batcher. I'll assign an eng lead and follow up with a timeline and recommended config changes.

I'll update you within 30 minutes with triage findings. Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize.

— Soojin
Soohjin (Soohjin) Lee
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Realtime API streaming latency — preliminary triage

On triage: observed correlated elevation in scheduling latency on a subset of US edge shards (edge-cluster-us-east-3) starting 08:42 UTC. Key observations:

- Continuous-batcher shim entered a slowpath when sequence length distribution spiked >512 tokens; the shim's batching window widened under a new kernel that rolled yesterday (kernel v2.4.7 -> v2.4.8).
- KV cache hit-rate for longer conversations dropped ~18% due to a small serialization change in the cache layer; higher cache-miss + larger batch windows amplified per-token latency for streaming responses.
- Throughput remained within normal bounds; this is a latency/ordering/scheduling regression rather than total capacity exhaustion.

Immediate mitigations we recommend to customers:
1) Route affected requests to the quantized fallback variant rwd-q4f (lower per-token CPU path) — we can do this server-side for FastChat.ai for a short window.
2) Toggle 'prefetch_prefix_kv'=true for your route to warm the KV cache where possible.
3) We'll perform a controlled rollback of the edge kernel on the affected nodes while leaving other clusters untouched.

I'll open INF-7829 and attach traces. If Soojin gives the go-ahead I can roll the routing override for FastChat.ai now.

--Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@fastchat.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-19T15:05:00Z
Subject: Post-incident summary: Realtime streaming slowdown (2026-08-18) — RCA and next steps

Hi Maya — follow-up with the post-incident summary and next steps. Thank you for your patience and for validating the temporary workaround. Below is a concise RCA and customer-facing guidance.

Incident timeline (UTC):
- 08:30 — Background kernel rolling update started in edge-cluster-us-east-3 (partial rollout).
- 08:42 — First telemetry alerts: scheduler tail-latency increase on streaming path.
- 08:50 — FastChat.ai reports user-visible lag; engineering triage begins.
- 09:05 — Identified batching shim slowpath and KV hit-rate regression; routing override prepared.
- 09:12 — Temporary routing override applied for FastChat.ai to rwd-q4f; immediate reduction in per-token latency observed (median dropped from ~55ms back to ~26ms).
- 09:35 — Kernel rollback initiated on affected shard group.
- 11:00 — Rollback completed; edge telemetry normalized across clusters.

Root cause summary: a kernel rollout introduced an unintended widening of the continuous-batcher window under certain sequence-length distributions, combined with a small cache-serialization change that reduced prefix KV hit-rate for longer conversations. The interaction of those two regressions amplified per-token scheduling latency on streaming endpoints. This is a software regresson in our runtime rollout process.

Customer impact and mitigation applied:
- Impact: FastChat.ai observed a 1.5–3x increase in token latency for ~1.1 hours on affected shards; ~12% sessions had user-visible lag.
- Mitigation: immediate routing override to rwd-q4f (applied for your account), enabling prefetch_prefix_kv where applicable, rollback of kernel on affected shard group.

Permanent remediation plan (next 30 days):
1) Add a preflight E2E streaming regression test in the kernel rollout pipeline that simulates broad sequence-length distributions and measures batching window behavior.
2) Revert the cache-serialization change to the previous stable implementation and add coverage in the KV integration tests.
3) Expose an account-level toggle for automatic fallback to quantized variants when tail-latency exceeds configured thresholds.
4) Publish an engineering postmortem and notify all customers with affected routes; we'll provide long-term timeline to opt into the automatic fallback.

SLA/credits: we will calculate your incident impact from our billing telemetry and follow Redwood's SLA policy. Ben Carter (cc'd) from Commercial will reach out with the credit estimate and next steps for procurement.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-rlive.pdf (draft), edges_grafana_08-18-2026.png (telemetry snapshot), streaming_traces_08-18-2026.log (trimmed traces)

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute wrap-up call this week to walk through the remediation plan and answer procurement questions.

Thanks again — we're treating this with high priority.

— Soojin
